hook: Poll an invented town of 20,000 whose true answer is hidden, then reveal it: a bigger sample shrinks the plus or minus, but a biased poll of 2,000 people can still be confidently wrong.
outcome: Explain how the way a sample is chosen and the way a question is worded bias a survey, estimate a proportion with a margin of error, and see why the margin of error covers only the luck of the draw
sources: Squire, Peverill (1988), "Why the 1936 Literary Digest Poll Failed," Public Opinion Quarterly 52(1): 125-133: https://doi.org/10.1086/269085
